The strangers' descriptions were far more positive. — разница большая, и говорящий это отмечает.

They were a bit more positive. — то же сравнение, но разница небольшая.

The finding is not nearly as controversial as the advert. — меньше, и намного. Именно разрыв здесь и важен.

options: The second sketch was slightly more positive.
The second sketch was far more positive.
The second sketch was a bit more positive.
steps.answer: The second sketch was far more positive.

steps.title: Как строится сравнение
steps.html:
МодельКогда используемПример
-er / more … thanсравнение двухThe second sketch was slimmer than the first.
the -est / the most …вершина группыIt's the most detailed painting in the room.
much / far / considerably / a lot + comparativeбольшая разницаfar more positive
slightly / a bit / a little + comparativeнебольшая разницаa bit more positive
(not) as … as / not nearly as … asстолько же или заметно меньшеnot nearly as controversial as the advert
by far the + superlativeвершина с явным отрывомby far the most different thing

steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Усилитель стоит перед сравнительной степенью: much better, far more positive, a bit older.

very не сочетается со сравнительной степенью. Very better — ошибка; нужно much.

В not as … as прилагательное остаётся в обычной форме: not as slim as.

Перед превосходной степенью — the; дальше in для места и of для группы: the tallest in the class.

steps.title: Художник рисует одно лицо дважды: по описанию самого человека и по описанию незнакомца. Чего вы ждёте?
How would you describe them?
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Абзац 4 разворачивается против самого эксперимента.

A few years ago an advertising team ran an experiment that is still worth thinking about. They hired a forensic artist — the kind who draws faces for the police from a witness's description — and put him behind a curtain. One at a time, women sat down on the other side and described their own faces to him. He never saw them. He drew what he heard.

Then each woman was sent into a room to talk to a stranger for a few minutes. Afterwards the stranger described her face to the same artist, and he drew a second picture. Nobody was told what the second sketch was for.

The two drawings were then put side by side. The difference was not small. One woman had described her own face as a lot more closed off, and fatter and sadder too; the stranger's version was slimmer, younger and, in her own words, far more open. The self-described faces had bigger chins, heavier eyebrows and thinner mouths. The strangers' descriptions were not kinder in a general way — they were simply more accurate, because the strangers had not spent thirty years looking at that face and remembering every flaw.

It is worth saying what the experiment does not prove. It was made by a company selling soap, the participants were not chosen at random, and nobody has repeated it under proper conditions. If you wanted to publish it as science, you could not.

But the finding it points at is not nearly as controversial as the advert. Ask people to describe themselves and they reach for what they dislike; ask a stranger who met them ten minutes ago and they reach for what they noticed. The face is the same one. The description is by far the most different thing in the room.

The description is by far the most different thing in the room.

items.text: He's got … hair, and a bit of a …
She's in her late thirties, I'd say.

steps.title: Ответьте вслух.
items: Опишите родственника тому, кто его не видел. Четыре предложения.
Теперь сравните его с собой дважды: с большой разницей и с маленькой.
Смогли бы вы точно описать своё лицо? Почему?

steps.title: Теперь опишите и сравните одним высказыванием. Запишите себя.
steps.sub: Используйте два усилителя и одно not as … as.
items: He's / She's much … than me, and slightly … .

steps.title: Урок 25 пройден
items: Я показываю величину разницы: much, far, slightly, a bit.
Я использую not as … as и by far the most.
Я при этом использую нереальное условие.
